title: Catholics under pressure today
hookLine: in some countries Christians practice their faith at real risk

lines: A BISHOP IN PRISON, THEN EXILE.
cards: Open an old calendar of martyrs and the scenes come easily: arenas, emperors, ancient Rome. Then open the news. In Nicaragua, a Catholic bishop, Rolando Álvarez, is sentenced to prison and later sent out of the country.
In Nigeria, a parish in the town of Owo is attacked during Mass on Pentecost Sunday. In other places, believers meet quietly, because meeting openly could cost them a job, their freedom, or more.
Those stories are still going on.

teach.b: The Church calls those killed for the faith martyrs. It keeps their names, and it is still adding to them.
The Acts of the Apostles tells of one of the earliest: Stephen, one of seven men the community chose to serve at its tables, stoned for what he preached.
As the stones fall, he prays for the men throwing them, asking the Lord not to hold this sin against them. The Gospel never promised otherwise.

In the Sermon on the Mount, in the Douay-Rheims, Jesus says: "Blessed are they that suffer persecution for justice' sake: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven." Pressure isn't treated as a sign that something went wrong.
It's named ahead of time. Then there's remembering.

teach.h: AS IF IN CHAINS WITH THEM.
teach.b: The letter to the Hebrews asks its readers to remember prisoners as if they were in chains alongside them, and those who suffer as people living in the same kind of body.
That is one reason Catholics in a quiet suburb pray for a parish in Nigeria or a bishop far from home: in that letter's picture, they are not strangers in a headline.

teach.h: QUIETER PRESSURE, AND NAMES SAID ALOUD.
teach.b: And pressure now? Sometimes it is violence.

teach.h: BLESSED ARE THEY THAT SUFFER PERSECUTION.
teach.b: Often, those who track it say, it is quieter: laws that close schools and charities, a job lost after a baptism, a priest followed by police, a church that can never get a building permit.

Believers of other faiths face it too, and the Second Vatican Council taught that religious freedom belongs to every person. Some parishes light their buildings red on a chosen day, red for the martyrs.
Others read names aloud at Mass, so they are not forgotten.

how: Catholics pray for persecuted Christians in the prayers of the faithful at Mass, some parishes light their churches red on a day of remembrance, and charities support communities under pressure.

games.q: you're a bishop in a country where preaching freely could mean prison. what do you do?
o: keep preaching, and stay with your people.
games.why: when the government put a group of prisoners on a flight out of the country, Bishop Rolando Álvarez refused to board. he was sentenced to prison, and later sent into exile.

practice: Bring to mind one place where believers practice at risk, from the news or from today; use a name if you know one, or picture one family getting dressed for Sunday, knowing what it might cost them.
In the same sermon, Jesus asks his listeners to pray for those who persecute them, too. If you pray, pray for both; if you don't, hold them all in mind with respect.

wordCard.voice: Martyr. The word for believers killed for their faith; Catholics under pressure today are the Church's newest witnesses, practicing at real risk.
